tweets.text:
God's eye view 24-hour replay of Operation Epic Fury.

The Iran strikes kicked off and I set an AI agent swarm loose to record every OSINT signal I could find before the caches cleared. Built a full 4D reconstruction in WorldView.

I can scrub through minute by minute and watch the whole thing unfold on a 3D globe:

> Airspace clearing over Tehran
> Ground strike coordinates locking in
> Severe GPS interference blinding the region
> EO and SAR satellites making passes over the strike zone
> No-fly zones locking down 9 countries
> Shipping fleets scrambling at the Strait of Hormuz

It's pretty amazing how complete of a picture you can build without "proprietary data fusion" -- one dev with public signals and a love for computer graphics and geospatial intelligence.

Thank you for all the love on my last post. Dropping WorldView in April. This my friends is just the beginning.

tweets.text:
Elon Musk just revealed what the $44 billion acquisition of Twitter was actually for.

For three years, the legacy media laughed. They said he overpaid for a dying social network. They said he destroyed the value. They said it was ego.

They were blind to what he actually believed.

He didn’t buy Twitter to make money. The math never made sense and he knew it.

He bought it because he believed that a single private company controlling the global flow of information was one of the most dangerous structures in the modern world.

And he was willing to spend $44 billion of his own money to dismantle it.

Musk: “The number of people who have the X app installed is well over a billion.”

Think about what a billion people with genuine free expression actually produces in real time.

Arguments. Discoveries. Market reactions. Political upheaval. Scientific debates. Grief. Rage. Revelation.

The full unfiltered spectrum of human thought, happening simultaneously, continuously, at a velocity no previous medium in history could capture.

For decades, the institutions that controlled information understood one thing: whoever shapes the narrative shapes reality.

Legacy media companies, social platforms, financial systems. They all built the exact same structure.

Centralized control. Moderation. Gatekeeping. The ability to decide what flows and what doesn’t.

They called it safety. It was leverage.

Musk watched them use it. Watched them throttle stories, suppress accounts, and quietly shape what billions of people were allowed to think and say.

He bought it to end that.

And in doing so, he accidentally created something nobody predicted.

You cannot build a maximal truth-seeking intelligence on a filtered internet.

Every content moderation decision is a gap in the model’s understanding of reality.

Every suppressed topic is a distortion baked into the foundation.

Every guardrail is a lie the AI learns as truth.

By protecting free speech, Musk guaranteed that Grok would train on raw, unfiltered human reality while every competitor trained their models on a curated, sanitized version of the world.

The idealism produced the strategic advantage. Not the other way around.

You are part of it. Right now. Reading this. Every post you’ve written on this platform. Every reaction. Every idea you put into words.

All of it flowing freely. The way it was supposed to.

Musk: “As we give people more reasons to use the X app, whether it’s for communications, for Grok or for X money, we want it to be such that, if you wanted to, you could live your life on the X app.”

Communication. Intelligence. Financial transactions. Every function a human being needs to operate in the modern world.

All inside one open ecosystem. All running on infrastructure built on the principle that information should flow freely and people should decide for themselves what to believe.

A billion humans expressing themselves without a gatekeeper deciding what’s allowed.

That’s not a training dataset. That’s what freedom actually looks like at scale.

They laughed at him for spending $44 billion on a website.

He bought the global public square and gave it back to the public.

The fact that it also happens to be the greatest AI training asset in human history is what happens when you build something real instead of something safe.

The gates the legacy world built to control the narrative are still standing.

Nobody is walking through them anymore.
